positive: Weak, diffuse positive activation on function words and continuation tokens in mid-sentence Wikipedia prose (prepositions like 'of'/'to' after verbs/adjectives, gerunds, plain nouns like 'crew', digits in date ranges); no strong single theme.
negative: Strong negative on military/warfare side-labels referring to the opposing or Allied side, especially ' Allied' (and ' Americans') after 'the'/'to' in WWII Pacific battle narratives (Guadalcanal etc.); also determiners/verbs in plans or operations against an enemy ('the' plan, 'repelling' infiltrators).

positive: Middle subword fragments of rare multi-token proper names, especially foreign/unusual surnames and unit names in military history text (e.g. 'egr' in Vandegrift, 'Squad' in Squadrons); mid-word name pieces.
negative: LaTeX closing braces and brace-adjacent tokens in math expressions: '}', '}}', '}_', '\' before right/rceil, closing a \frac, \sqrt, \boxed, \underbrace argument.

positive: Food item words in math word problems, especially snack/cooked foods after a quantity or 'of'/'the' (fried chicken, nuts, peanut butter, toast); also occasional chemistry subword like 'ich' in trichloride.
negative: Second subword of vegetable/plant words, notably 'atoes' in Tomatoes in bulleted math reasoning lists; also place/name endings in titles (Merchant of Venice) and descriptive nouns in botany (mushroom 'bell').

positive: Tokens at the end of a header/opening phrase just before content begins: the 'to'/'for' in 'Here's a thinking process to/for solving' at the start of <think>; newline after section headings (= = = X = = =) or list items in Wikipedia; sentence-final periods.
negative: Indentation whitespace and bullet markers ('   ', ' *') at the start of a new nested bullet line in markdown-formatted step-by-step math reasoning, and double newlines before the next numbered step.

positive: First/early subword tokens of foreign proper names (places, ships, people) where the name is being spelled out (Tysfjorden, Transvaal, Poltava, Erik Satie); also 'answer' in the 'put your final answer within \boxed' prompt.
negative: Math/code tokens introducing a value: '$' dollar sign right after 'equal to', '=', 'was' in money calculations in reasoning traces; ' =' after a \text{} label; closing '),' in Asymptote draw code.

positive: First token of a hyphenated compound (followed by ' @-@') or a multi-word title/name: 'long' in long-term/long-lasting, 'self' in self-defence, 'Long' in title 'At Long Last', first part of exotic place names (Tagaung).
negative: First token of compound or directional geographic names: ' South' in South Korea/South Pacific/South Korean, 'fly' in flyover, 'hang' before @-@ (hang-out); directional/compound-starting words in Wikipedia text.

positive: Digits, decimal points, thousands-separator commas and ' =' inside numeric computations in math reasoning (multi-digit products like 1,080,000, 70.71), and sentence-initial names starting a word problem.
negative: Very strong on sentence/clause-final punctuation ('.', ').', ' ,') at the end of a bullet line in markdown reasoning traces, immediately followed by a newline and next bullet '*'; end-of-statement punctuation.

positive: Common nouns or name completions in Wikipedia narrative that complete a noun phrase after 'the'/a name (border war, Tokyo Dome, Escalators, police, gubernatorial); generic topic nouns.
negative: Second token of organization/company/institution names, especially media and entertainment entities (Warner Bros, ZDF, Pinewood Studios, Capitol Records, United Nations).

positive: Function words in hedged/subordinate or passive constructions continuing a clause: 'been' after 'have', 'if' after 'even', 'process' in 'Here's a thinking process', 'ones' in 'are the ones', copula after a descriptive subject phrase.
negative: Copula 'was'/'is' immediately after a simple subject pronoun or name (he was, Starr was, Father is, side length is) describing a state or value, in both biography narration and math checks.

positive: Digits (or the space before a number) in large quantities/statistics in Wikipedia: box office grosses, funding amounts, sales figures, viewership, circulation, typically the first digits after '$', '£', 'over', 'about' preceding '@,@' or 'million'.
negative: Forms of the verb 'turn' (turned, turn, turning), especially 'turned back', 'turning on', 'turned to'.
